newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end higher after erasing losses toward close.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end higher after erasing losses toward close.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended higher on Wednesday due to short-covering, traders said.

"Those who had earlier sold for hedging purposes ahead of the Bank of Japan governor's news conference bought back after seeing that JGBs had a solid bottom," said a trader for a city bank's securities unit.
Speculation that the BOJ governor was not likely to say anything new in his assessment of the economy helped trigger a spate of short-covering, traders said.
The September ended at 124.95, up from Tuesday's close of 124.75. Turnover was 28,309 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.280 percent as of 0623 GMT, down from Tuesday's close of 2.315 percent.
JGBs fell in early morning trade as it retained weakness after falling on LIFFE overnight and because of a surge in Tokyo share prices, traders said.

But target buying of cash bonds, which involves selling of out-of-the-money JGB put options, were detected when JGBs fell, and provided support on the downside, said a trader for a second-tier brokerage house.
"The target buying led to a view that there is demand for cash bonds on dips," the trader said.

In target buying trades, sellers of put options will be able to obtain the desired JGB issue if the market falls and the put options come in the money. If they expire without being executed, the writer of the option gets the premium from having sold the put option.

"There was also demand for the 197th 2.6 percent 10-year JGB at par...which is roughly equal to 124.50 (of the key September contract)," the second trader said. Such demand supported JGBs at 124.50, he said.

BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita said after the close of JGB futures trade on Wednesday that the central bank will continue to conduct its monetary policy with the aim of strengthening the basis for economic recovery,

Matsushita told a news conference although Japan's economy continues to be affected by a rise in the sales tax in April, the economy as a whole is continuing to recover gradually and this was confirmed by a meeting of BOJ branch managers this week.
"For the time being we will continue to carry out monetary policy putting emphasis on economic recovery," Matsushita said.
